annotation.title_clean: Humanoids in STEM outreach: a framework for responsible deployment through engaged research
annotation.title_en: Humanoids in STEM outreach: a framework for responsible deployment through engaged research
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Delgado, M.; Connolly, C.; O'Keeffe, D.T.
annotation.summary_en: Perspective article reporting 2025 field deployments of a Unitree G1 humanoid in Irish schools and a charity event. It identifies physical safety, anthropomorphism, privacy and regulatory-gap concerns, and argues for governance-first deployment, including age-gating, kinematic buffer zones, constrained LLM speech and operator control.
key_provisions_or_claims: Full-size humanoids in schools need governance-first rather than pedagogy-first deployment.
Age-gate full-size humanoids, suited to older primary and secondary students, not under-tens.
Establish kinematic buffer zones (e.g. 2 m) around high-mass robots.
Constrain LLM speech and keep operators able to intervene at any time.
Existing frameworks (Machinery Regulation, ISO 13482, GDPR, AI Act) cover only parts of the system, leaving a regulatory gap.
